items.impact: Provides a uniform certifiable command path with projected availability, disabled-state communication, dispatch correlation, canonical effects, and accessibility evidence.
items.statement: The orchestrator controls define dispatcher registration, typed command responses, projected availability and disabled reasons, correlated event or receipt effects, and keyboard/focus/assistive-technology evidence as certification requirements.
items.title: Orchestrator controls have a common production wiring contract

evidence.exact_quote: "description": "cmd.orchestrator.restore_safe_point_then_retry has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition.",

items.impact: A restore-and-retry operation could target the wrong run or safe point, race with active work, or partially restore state without a defined authorization, confirmation, rollback, or recovery oracle.
items.statement: The restore-safe-point-then-retry command is reduced to a generic no-persist receipt or route/open disposition; the row does not identify the run and safe point, define authority or confirmation, specify atomicity against concurrent execution, or state rollback and partial-restore behavior.
items.title: Restore-safe-point safety and recovery semantics are missing

evidence.exact_quote: "description": "cmd.orchestrator.push_image has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition.",
"description": "cmd.orchestrator.switch_tab has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition.",

items.impact: Implementations and tests cannot distinguish navigation completion from a potentially long-running image push, including progress, cancellation, network loss, remote rejection, or partial completion.
items.statement: Operationally different commands such as push_image and switch_tab share the same generic no-persist receipt or route/open effect language, without operation-specific outputs, terminal states, or failure and retry semantics.
items.title: Generic receipt language obscures operation-specific effects

"description": "cmd.panel.switch has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition.",

items.impact: Separates durable redock and undock layout changes from a no-persist panel switch while retaining common dispatch, state-projection, accessibility, and evidence requirements.
items.statement: Panel redock and undock emit canonical layout events, while panel switch records a no-persist disposition; each row also binds a handler, availability selector, disabled reason, accessibility behavior, and event or receipt oracle.
items.title: Panel controls distinguish durable layout events from switching

items.impact: Untrusted or oversized persona files could be accepted ambiguously, leak sensitive configuration on export, fail partway, or migrate incompatibly without a testable compatibility and recovery contract.

evidence.exact_quote: "Plan Compile command is pre-enable/design-only unless Plans/Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md, Executor_Protocol, and Goal_Runtime_System explicitly enable runtime activation; it must not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, runtime dispatch, implementation files, or production build tasks.",

items.impact: Prevents UI wiring and receipts from being mistaken for authorization to create executable planning artifacts or launch build/runtime work.
items.statement: Plan Compile cancel and inspection commands are explicitly design-only until three named owner documents enable runtime activation, with WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, queues, dispatch, implementation files, and build tasks expressly forbidden.
items.title: Plan Compile pre-enable boundary is explicit and testable

evidence.exact_quote: "effect_kind": "route_open",

"description": "cmd.plan_compile.open_build opens the resulting build/artifact route when a build identity exists, or records a disabled route/open receipt while runtime activation remains blocked; it must not fabricate plan_compile.command_applied.",

items.impact: Gives inspection and lifecycle controls observable receipts and makes open_build a distinct route effect that cannot fabricate a domain event.
items.statement: Plan Compile blocker and evidence inspection, pause, bounded recompile, resume, and retry use explicit receipts, while open_build uses a route_open receipt gated on build identity and runtime activation; all carry state and accessibility evidence obligations.
items.title: Plan Compile controls distinguish receipts from route opening

evidence.exact_quote: "cmd.plan_compile.retry must expose projected state selector and disabled reason before dispatch",
"description": "cmd.plan_compile.retry records an explicit no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition; placeholder command_applied events are invalid.",

items.impact: Pause, resume, retry, and bounded recompile can race or be repeated against stale runs with no specified idempotency, ordering, partial-failure recovery, or support-visible terminal outcome.
items.statement: The Plan Compile lifecycle rows expose only generic availability, disabled reason, and receipt contracts; they do not define run identity and revision, legal source and target states, duplicate-command behavior, mutual exclusion, cancellation interaction, retry budget, or rollback after partial work.
items.title: Plan Compile lifecycle transitions and race rules are absent

evidence.exact_quote: "evidence_required": "Production wiring contract for cmd.plan_compile.open_build; Production certification requires render/control evidence, dispatcher fixture, typed payload/result assertion, projected state selector, disabled-reason proof, receipt/event assertion, accessibility check, and regression test evidence. Disabled/pre-enable disposition: this row covers UI contract shape only and cannot certify runtime launch/build effects while PlanCompile runtime activation remains disabled.",

items.impact: Users could interpret an available-looking Open Build control or a route receipt as proof that executable build work exists, especially with stale identity, failed routing, or offline state.
items.statement: Although the row states that UI contract evidence cannot certify runtime launch or build effects, it does not define the visible mutually exclusive states and copy that distinguish no build identity, durable pre-enable identity, disabled runtime, stale identity, route failure, loading, and an actually openable artifact.
items.title: Open Build needs explicit non-misleading GUI states

evidence.exact_quote: "Final-review CAS fields match the displayed ApprovedPlanPack, PlanningRun, topic map, index, testing policy, and audit/closure hashes",
"Duplicate idempotency key returns the same PlanCompileRun identity and does not create a second ordinary launch",
"Orchestrator Plan Compile opens pending-launch state and binds to durable PlanCompileRun without tab-switch-only success",

items.impact: Prevents stale approval, duplicate ordinary launches, and false success based only on navigation while preserving a durable pre-enable run identity.
items.statement: Approve And Build has unusually strong acceptance oracles: displayed final-review hashes must match CAS fields, an idempotency-key replay returns the same PlanCompileRun, and success requires durable pending-launch binding rather than a tab switch.
items.title: Approve And Build defines CAS, idempotency, and durable-binding oracles

items.impact: A crash or conflict between receipt, approval, and run-binding writes could expose an approved plan without a bound run, a run without durable approval, or an idempotency replay with ambiguous repair behavior.
items.statement: The row requires three correlated event types but does not define their transaction boundary, causal order, visibility point, deduplication across partial emission, or recovery and rollback if only a prefix is durable.
items.title: Approve And Build multi-event atomicity is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: "description": "cmd.planning_wizard.amendment.accept records an explicit no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition; placeholder command_applied events are invalid.",
"description": "cmd.planning_wizard.topic.merge records an explicit no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition; placeholder command_applied events are invalid.",

items.impact: Accept, add, defer, mark-impacted, and merge actions can change planning meaning without a specified durable result, authorization boundary, conflict strategy, undo path, downstream invalidation, or user-visible recovery state.
items.statement: Planning Wizard amendment and topic mutations are modeled as generic no-persist receipts even for merge and impact changes; their target identities, before-and-after states, persistence authority, consumer propagation, concurrent-edit handling, confirmation, undo, and partial-failure behavior are not defined.
items.title: Planning Wizard mutations lack durable semantic effects and safety rules

segments.summary: Reviewed orchestrator pause, preview, image-push, safe-point retry, resume, and tab-switch wiring; captured the common contract and destructive/effect-taxonomy gaps.
Reviewed panel redock/switch/undock and persona create/delete/duplicate wiring; captured event distinctions and destructive lifecycle and identity gaps.
Reviewed persona export/import/select/update and Plan Compile cancel/assignment inspection; captured canonical events, transfer trust gaps, and the explicit pre-enable boundary.
Reviewed Plan Compile blocker/evidence inspection, open-build, pause, bounded-recompile, resume, and retry wiring; captured route semantics, lifecycle races, and GUI truth gaps.
Reviewed Planning Wizard amendment, approval/build, start, and topic mutation wiring; captured strong CAS/idempotency oracles plus atomicity and durable-mutation gaps.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner defines concrete payload, result, error, permission, and idempotency schemas for these UICommand rows?
Which canonical owner defines the legal PlanCompileRun lifecycle, command race policy, partial-failure repair, and support-visible terminal states?
Which canonical owner defines persona import/export format, migration, untrusted-input limits, secret redaction, and delete/duplicate lifecycle semantics?
Are Planning Wizard amendment and topic mutations intentionally receipt-only, or must a durable planning-domain effect and consumer invalidation contract be declared?
How must the GUI distinguish a durable pre-enable PlanCompileRun identity from an executable build and from stale, offline, or failed route states?
